relationships.detail: The non-reference end face has a parallelism control referencing datum A.
The parallelism control establishes the non-reference end face parallel to the datum A reference face.
Section A-A identifies nBS II and BS I as the opposing annular end faces.
The groove position and parallelism controls reference datum A.
The groove position control references datum B, established by the external lug crest cylinder.
The groove position control references datum C, the centerplane of the designated indexing lug within the external lug pattern.
Section A-A controls the groove centerline plane parallel to datum A.
The outer relief step has a circular runout control referencing datum B.
Circular runout of the relief step is controlled about the datum B axis.
The external lug width and angular pattern position controls reference datum A.
The external lug width and angular pattern position controls reference datum B.

The angular pattern position control references datum C carried by the designated indexing lug within this compound pattern feature; this edge represents an internal datum reference, not an additional lug instance.
The outer rim runout controls reference datum A.
The outer rim runout controls reference datum B.
Runout of the cylindrical rim between the lugs is controlled about the datum B axis.
The internal gear tip-circle runout control references datum B.
The internal gear tip-circle runout is controlled about the datum B axis.
The internal gearing and external crest cylinder share the ring gear rotation axis Z.
The continuous outer circumferential groove is centered about the external cylinder and ring gear axis.
The annular part body and internal gearing share the world Z rotation axis.
The front view explicitly defines equally spaced external drive lugs around the outer circumference and common rotation axis.
The isometric observation explicitly shows the circumferential groove dividing the external dogs into two axial tiers.
Detail Y and Section A-A locate the groove in the external cylindrical surface.
The root transition fillet meets the side flank of the external lug.
The root transition fillet joins the external lug flank to the outer cylinder between lugs.
The BS-side entry chamfer is formed on the reference-side ends of the internal teeth.
The nBS-side entry chamfer is formed on the non-reference-side ends of the internal teeth.
The reference-side tooth entry chamfer meets the BS I annular end face.
The non-reference-side tooth entry chamfer meets the nBS II annular end face.
The standard tip-chamfer configuration modifies the internal gear tooth tip-to-flank transition.
The alternative tip-chamfer configuration modifies the same internal tooth tip zone if that configuration is selected; it is not established as an additional simultaneous operation.
The revolving deburr requirement applies along internal gear tooth tip, flank, and root boundaries.
The DMC marking patch is on the rear, negative-Z annular end face corresponding to nBS II.
The two tooth entry chamfers are explicitly assigned to opposing BS I and nBS II ends.

datum_scheme.datum_hierarchy_notes: The A-B-C position frames establish A as the primary reference end plane, B as the secondary axis derived from the external lug crest cylinder, and C as the tertiary angular indexing centerplane of the designated lug. Datum C is carried within the compound external lug pattern node. Other controls reference A alone, B alone, or A-B as explicitly shown. The gear-table inspection reference GG is not defined by the supplied section graphs and remains subject to clarification.

component_specs.extraction_notes: The table specifies an internal gear (labeled 'internal gear' in the column header) calculated with KISSsoft 03/2017 B. Parameters 10, 18.2, 19.12, and 19.19 are marked with inspection oval flag 51. Several section titles (11, 12.0, 18.0, 20.00, 20.10, 20.30) span the table and define sub-sections.

component_spec_links.link_notes: These observations describe the same internal Laufverzahnung tooth zone. The table establishes its internal helical gear identity and supplies the symbolic gear diameters, tooth parameters, and inspection requirements referenced by the views. The external drive dogs are a separate feature and are not linked to this table.

assumptions.text: Grouped the datum B lug crest observation with the Ø221.1 external cylinder observations. The crest is the outer tip cylinder, whereas the separately dimensioned Ø213.9 cylinder is explicitly between the lugs. This surface-identity decision uses the descriptions and spatial context; no diameter was extracted from the images.

Selected detail_y:F1 as the external crest cylinder canonical because it supplies the toleranced diameter, axial length, explicit Z axis, and cylindricity control. Its dimensions agree with section_aa:F3; the section's radial axis label was not preferred over the axial cylinder orientation in Detail Y.

Represented the external dogs as one compound 50-instance pattern rather than separately modelling the detail lug and the remaining dogs. Detail Z is the linked representative enlargement and also identifies the selected indexing lug centerplane as datum C. The front-view canonical preserves the explicit pattern count and angular spacing. No aggregate_refs were used because the individual dogs are not separately enumerated elsewhere.

Grouped all observations of the unique internal tooth zone, including the hardness evaluation schematic. The front-view section and detail links anchor this identity; the isometric and hardness observations describe that same internal gearing, not additional splines. Hardness evaluation dimensions remain inspection-location callouts rather than alternative manufacturing diameters.

Selected detail_y:F4 as the internal gear canonical for its detailed radial and axial annotations, but deliberately sourced length_mm and depth_condition from section_aa:F5. The 23.4 Lβ annotation is treated as the flank-line regression length identified by the gear table, not as a conflicting replacement for the 26 overall through-tooth extent. The two 1.3 offsets also support this distinction.

Treated the Ø194.1 annotation in Detail Y as the theoretical/root evaluation circle corroborated by hardness_evaluation:F1, not as the finished gear tip diameter. The gear table explicitly supplies the finished tip diameter separately. Sourced the merged gear description from section_aa:F5 to avoid carrying forward Detail Y's conflicting tip-diameter wording; all extracted callouts remain preserved.

Grouped isometric_view:F5 with the BS I datum A face because both are the accessible +Z annular end face. The rear DMC patch instead belongs to the opposing -Z nBS II face and remains a separate marking feature.

Grouped front_view:F3 with detail_z:F3 using the matching between-lugs cylinder description and shared A-B datum references. Preferred the explicitly toleranced detail observation. The front-view zero runout entry is an extraction placeholder for symbolic Fr, whose value is supplied by the gear table; it was not interpreted as a zero-tolerance requirement.

Kept tip_chamfer:F1 and tip_chamfer:F2 ungrouped because they are explicitly presented as standard and alternative configurations. Their matching angle and symbolic diameters do not establish that they are simultaneous physical features; configuration selection remains open.

Kept detail_y:F3 as a separate relief-step singleton and did not substitute its diameter for the groove bottom diameter. The supplied observations describe a shoulder step but do not establish that it is the groove floor.
The tooth tip chamfers conform to the standard configuration designated by tip_chamfer:F1.
The undimensioned outer rim corners identified in Detail Y are deburred only, with no discrete chamfer feature applied.
The bottom diameter of the outer circumferential groove is Ø207.1 ± 0.1 mm, which corresponds to a nominal radial depth of 7.0 mm from the Ø221.1 outer diameter.
The Ø207.1 dimension defines the bottom diameter of the outer groove/relief step, which has an axial extent (width) of 3.18 mm (+0.12/-0.02 mm).

GG designates the 3.18 mm wide circumferential groove (or its toleranced flanks) located on the Ø221.1 outer diameter in Detail Y, which serves as an axial reference feature for gear measurement alongside datums A and B.
